messages:
alex: Heads-up — bulk claim reconciliation job just ran and ~1.8k keys got reattributed to the wrong projects. Console shows them under 'project-legacy-42'.
priya: omg, that's the job that maps SA claims -> project. What signal did it use?
sam: Any errors in the job logs? Could be a batching race with the update pipeline.
alex: It used the recent heuristic: prefer origin_project if present, else origin_org -> project lookup. Looks like origin_project was populated with an old transient id.
lena: That transient id issue is from the onboarding flow that wrote temp_project during provisioning. We should have normalized on final_project_id.
jamie: Also: telemetry shows quota attribution spikes against the wrong billing org for the affected keys. Finance pinged us.
priya: Reconciliation is dangerous w/o a dry-run. Does the job support dry-run mode? We should have flagged it.
alex: It does, but dry-run was disabled in the scheduled cron (we flipped to reduce read ops).
sam: Logs show a lot of write_conflict retries on the batch updater. snippet: ```sql
UPDATE claims SET project_id = $1 WHERE id = $2 RETURNING id, project_id
```
lena: That batching approach was changed in canary last week (PR 4867). Maybe we need to revert the batch-window tweak.
jamie: For rollback: create DB migration to map project -> previous_project (we store previous_project_id in audit log). Then replay for affected keys.
priya: We should also add a quick telemetry guard: compare pre/post billing attribution totals by org and alert on >1% drift. Finance impact could be big.
alex: Agreed. Action items: pause job, run targeted dry-run, compute diff, and revert wrong attributions. I can coordinate the revert once we have diffs.
sam: I can pause the scheduler. Will do it at 11:05 UTC and run a targeted dry-run for the affected project prefix.
infra-bot: job scheduler: bulk-claim-reconciliation paused by sam at 1729456820 :white_check_mark:
jamie: I'll prepare the DB rollback migration and a console hotfix to hide reattributed keys until audit completes.
lena: I'll open an incident in #incidents and ping finance + product.
priya: Follow-up tasks: (1) revert batch-window (PR 4867), (2) re-run dry-run full, (3) run automated billing snapshot check, (4) improve telemetry to detect sudden org-attribution drift and anomalous write_conflicts.
alex: I'll draft a short postmortem and an immediate checklist for running reconciliation jobs (include dry-run default ON, sample size checks, billing-snapshot preflight).
priya: also let's add a canary gate that runs the reconciliation on a 0.1% sample and validates no billing drift before full run.
jamie: I'll include a reversible transaction plan so we can run a single SQL to rollback in emergencies.
priya: thanks. cc @rohan (billing) for visibility.
rohan: Thanks for the ping — finance is looking into reported spike, please include the org-level CSV export in the incident.
alex: Will attach exports and the dry-run diffs to the incident.
priya: Can one of you own the post-change monitoring ticket? Something that checks org attribution every 5m for 24h after runs.
sam: I'll own the monitoring ticket and add the alert to the routing dashboard.
lena: Keeping this open until the DB migration and telemetry guards are in prod.
priya: Great. TL;DR: job paused, dry-run in progress, rollback plan being prepared, batch-window revert + telemetry improvements queued.
